subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should OpenClaw solve this WhatsApp `inter_session` delivery-loss symptom with the narrow requester-return-path prompt contract from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311, or wait for the broader structured callback design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478?
rationale: The remaining choice is not whether suppression exists in source; it is which model-facing A2A delivery contract maintainers want because the current placeholder prompt was intentionally added for prompt-cache stability.

options.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate and require focused security/message-delivery review plus WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to structured callbacks
options.body: Keep this issue open but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478 the design owner for a typed callback or delivery-intent contract instead of prompt-level guidance.

options.title: Request fresh live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on a current-main WhatsApp transcript if maintainers are not comfortable changing A2A prompt semantics from source evidence and the candidate PR proof alone.

recommendation.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate and require focused security/message-delivery review plus WhatsApp or equivalent source-reply proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on `sessions_send` A2A delivery and maintainer-visible area history make this the best available routing candidate for the product contract choice.
